First of all, for making me a witness to the apparition of our Blessed Mother,
I offer a thousand thanks to our Blessed Mother and her Divine Son.
My name is Rani, and this is my husband, Raju, and we belong to St. Joseph's Parish in Chirakkal.
I made the Covenant in 2022.
I am sharing this testimony on behalf of my husband.
My husband used to experience frequent chest pains and shortness of breath.
As he was having a lot of difficulty, we went to the hospital and did an angiogram test.
After the tests, the doctor advised an angiogram, and it revealed a 90% block.
They strongly recommended a bypass surgery.
Since my husband was not willing to undergo a bypass surgery, we asked for an angioplasty, but the doctor refused.
He said there was no point in doing that and a bypass was strictly necessary, so we went to another hospital.
When we consulted the doctor there, he said an angioplasty could be done despite some risks.
He agreed to do the angioplasty, and thus, on August 4th, the procedure began.
Right in the middle of the angioplasty procedure, he suffered a massive heart attack.
The heart attack made his condition extremely critical, and time stood still.
When they finally brought my husband out of the theater, he had no breath left in him.
His eyes were barely open, and he looked completely lifeless.
They brought him out in a highly critical state, and I desperately asked the doctor what had happened.
The doctor explained that a heart attack occurred during the angioplasty, and his condition was dire.
He was being moved to a ventilator, and my husband slightly opened his eyes and just looked at me.
The doctors rushed him to the ventilator, and after about half an hour, the doctor came out.
He told us his condition was extremely critical, saying, "We have done everything we can; there is nothing more left in our hands."
His BP had dropped drastically, his heart's pumping was very weak, and all his vital organs had almost failed.
He was 99% clinically dead, and they told me I could go in and see him if I wanted to.
When I went inside, his eyes were covered with cotton, his mouth was slightly open, and he laid there stiff.
He looked almost exactly like a corpse, and I could only bear to take one look at him.
The doctor kept saying things, but I couldn't even pay attention, so I quickly went back to our room.
My younger brother, his daughter, and my elder sister were with me, and my brother asked what went wrong.
He said, "He went in looking so calm, what happened all of a sudden?", to which the doctor explained about the massive heart attack.
The doctor said there was no hope of survival, as he was completely unresponsive and surrounded entirely by life-support machines.
He was only being kept alive by those machines.
They said they had done everything they possibly could, while many doctors surrounded him, trying various procedures.
After about an hour had passed, they advised us to inform all our relatives.
They are nine siblings in total, and when everyone arrived, the doctor told them there was no hope left.
He said they would take him off the ventilator by 10 AM the next day, and told us to prepare to take the body. There's no more hope, they said.
I immediately called my sister's son and daughter-in-law and told them, "I need to go to Kreupasanam in the morning."
I told them I must go and pray at the feet of our Blessed Mother, and they arrived early, around 6 AM.
My nephew, his wife, and I came straight to Kreupasanam, entering the presence of our Blessed Mother.
I went straight to the feet of our Blessed Mother and prayed, "I have come to beg for my husband's life."
That was all I said; I didn't utter another word, but simply looked at Mother and wept bitterly.
My sister's daughter-in-law was standing right next to me, and a phone call came from the hospital.
I knew instantly it was from them, and I stood near her but didn't ask anything.
Only after the call did she speak to me, bearing all her sorrow to break the news.
